scope: Single-host 32-byte slices of one immutable record per run; baseline/fixed installed wheels, serial ABBA batches, plain/stage/libc modes. No new physical 100 GB or TB run.
limitations: Plain means the installed API path is unmodified; caller boundary clocks and resource counters still measure it. Stage/libc modes alter timing and are not interchangeable with plain latency.

Sequential ABBA reduces ordering differences but does not isolate host-wide load or evict caches. The same first 32 bytes are read repeatedly from repeating uint8 data. This is not physical bandwidth or random-position correctness evidence.

The interposer reports selected libc calls under an exact private absolute root and tracked descriptors. It does not cover all possible syscalls, relative openat paths, dup or other threads; coverage is checked for this probe only.

Wall minus thread CPU includes storage blocking, kernel waiting, scheduling and other blocking. Time inside open64 does not identify a metadata RPC, network or server bottleneck. errno is meaningful only on failure.
No new retry deadline, VisibleBy value, fairness assumption or bandwidth SLA follows. CPU/wall clocks are sampled separately and tiny residuals can include clock sampling skew.

Runtime I/O adapters remain unproved. No production optimization or new correctness bug is claimed; two opens per uncached read identify a concrete optimization candidate that must preserve fresh opens on retry and byte authentication.
Three new runs reclaim fixtures with normal GC after child readers exit; prior stage-only runs retain their own source hashes and are separately archived.
